A collection of my technical blog posts and articles published across various platforms.

## Blog Posts (amaarora.github.io)

1. [An Introduction to Real-Time Guardrails & Qwen3Guard](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2025-09-25-qwen3guard-guardrails.html): A comprehensive technical review and introduction to Qwen3Guard, exploring how it addresses critical limitations in existing guardrail models through controversial classification, real-time streaming detection, and multilingual safety moderation across 119 languages.
2. [How LLMs Scaled from 512 to 2M Context: A Technical Deep Dive](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2025-09-21-rope-context-extension.html): A comprehensive technical guide through the evolution of positional encodings such as APE, RoPE, Position Interpolation, NTK-Aware Scaling, Dynamic Scaling, and YaRN in Large Language Models.
3. [What Makes Modern Day LLMs Agentic](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2025-09-14-llms-agentic.html): Demystifying tool calling in LLMs - how special tokens and training patterns create the illusion of agency, when it's really just next token prediction with clever scaffolding.
4. [Claude's New File Capabilities - My Notes and Reflections](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2025-09-10-claude-file-capabilities.html): Exploring Claude's new file handling features and their implications for AI-assisted development.
5. [Agent Frameworks Are So Much More Than For Loops](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2025-09-08-agent-frameworks-more-than-loops.html): A deep dive into what makes modern agent frameworks powerful beyond simple iteration.
6. [Deciphering LangChain: A Deep Dive into Code Complexity](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2023-07-25-llmchain.html): An analysis of LangChain's architecture and code complexity.
7. [Paper Review - 'LaMini-LM'](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2023-04-30_LaMini-LM.html): A review of the paper "LaMini-LM - A Diverse Herd of Distilled Models from Large-Scale Instructions".
9. [The Annotated CLIP (Part-2)](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2023-03-11_Understanding_CLIP_part_2.html): A detailed explanation of the PyTorch code behind CLIP for model building and training.
10. [The Annotated CLIP (Part-1)](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2023-03-06_Understanding_CLIP.html): An introduction to CLIP, comparing it to other research papers and discussing the inspiration behind it.
11. [Swin Transformer](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2022-07-04-swintransformerv1.html): Explanation and PyTorch implementation of the Swin Transformer Model Architecture.
5. [The Annotated DETR](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-07-26-annotateddetr.html): Explanation and PyTorch implementation of the DETR Model Architecture for end-to-end object detection.
6. [The sad state of AI and tech startups in Australia today and what can we do about it](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-05-15-jh-meetup.html): A discussion on the current state of AI and tech startups in Australia.
7. [Adam and friends](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-03-13-optimizers.html): Implementation of basic optimizers like Adam, SGD, RMSProp from scratch in PyTorch.
8. [Vision Transformer](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-01-18-ViT.html): Detailed look at the Vision Transformer architectures and their re-implementation in PyTorch from scratch.
9. [The EfficientDet Architecture in PyTorch](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-01-13-efficientdet-pytorch.html): A guide on how to implement the EfficientDet architecture in PyTorch from scratch.
10. [EfficientDet - Scalable and Efficient Object Detection](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2021-01-11-efficientdet.html): Explanation of how EfficientDets work step-by-step.
11. [U-Net A PyTorch Implementation in 60 lines of Code](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-09-13-unet.html): Implementation of the U-Net architecture in PyTorch in 60 lines of code.
12. [Top 100 solution - SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax Segmentation](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-09-06-siimacr.html): A solution for Image Segmentation based problem in Pytorch with SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax Segmentation competition.
13. [GeM Pooling Explained with PyTorch Implementation and Introduction to Image Retrieval](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-08-30-gempool.html): Explanation of GeM pooling and implementation from scratch in PyTorch.
14. [SIIM-ISIC Melanoma Classification - my journey to a top 5% solution and first silver medal on Kaggle](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-08-23-siimisic.html): Sharing of winning solution for SIIM-ISIC Melanoma Classification Kaggle Competition.
15. [EfficientNet](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-08-13-efficientnet.html): A look at the current SOTA, with top-1 accuracy of 88.5% on ImageNet.
16. [Group Normalization](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-08-09-groupnorm.html): A look at Group Normalization research paper and implementation in PyTorch from scratch.
17. [DenseNet Architecture Explained with PyTorch Implementation from TorchVision](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-08-02-densenets.html): Introduction to dense blocks, transition layers and the TorchVision implementation of DenseNet step-by-step.
18. [Squeeze and Excitation Networks Explained with PyTorch Implementation](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-07-24-SeNet.html): Re-implementation of the Squeeze-and-Excitation networks in PyTorch step-by-step with very minor updates to ResNet implementation.
19. [Label Smoothing Explained using Microsoft Excel](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-07-18-label-smoothing.html): Re-implementation of Label Smoothing in Microsoft Excel step by step.
20. [An introduction to PyTorch Lightning with comparisons to PyTorch](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-07-12-oganized-pytorch.html): An introduction to Pytorch Lightning and implementation of all the cool tricks like - Gradient Accumulation, 16-bit precision training, and also add TPU/multi-gpu support - all in a few lines of code.
21. [What is Focal Loss and when should you use it?](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-06-29-FocalLoss.html): Understanding what Focal Loss is and when it is used, including a deep dive into its math and step-by-step implementation in PyTorch.
22. [The Annotated GPT-2](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-02-18-The_Annotated_GPT-2.html): An annotated version of the GPT-2 paper in the form of a line-by-line implementation in PyTorch.
